name: Granby roll to reverse position
description: Master the Granby roll to reverse position from Leg Knot Bottom. Escape leg entanglement and achieve top position. Success rates: Beginner 30%, Intermediate 50%, Advanced 65%.
overview:
The Granby roll to reverse position is a dynamic escape and reversal technique from Leg Knot Bottom that uses rotational momentum to disengage from the opponent's leg entanglement and achieve a dominant position. This movement capitalizes on the transitional nature of the Leg Knot position, where neither player has fully consolidated control, creating windows for athletic inversions that can completely reverse the positional hierarchy.

Strategically, the Granby roll serves as both an escape mechanism when facing leg lock threats and an offensive tool for gaining top position. The technique exploits the natural gaps created during leg entanglement exchanges, using shoulder-driven rotation to clear the trapped leg while simultaneously repositioning to threaten the opponent's legs. Unlike linear escape methods that fight directly against the entanglement, the Granby roll uses circular motion to unwind the leg configuration.

The key to success lies in precise timing and commitment to the rotation. Attempting the Granby roll against a fully consolidated opponent will fail, but executing it during transitions or grip adjustments can catch even experienced leg lockers off guard. The movement requires significant shoulder flexibility and core strength, making it a higher-level technique that rewards practitioners who invest in athletic development alongside technical study.
key_principles: Initiate the roll from the shoulders, not the hips - shoulder rotation generates the momentum needed to clear the trapped leg
Time the movement during opponent's grip adjustments or positional transitions when control is momentarily weakened
Maintain a tight, compact body position throughout the roll to prevent opponent from re-establishing grips
Keep the trapped leg limp during initial rotation, then explosively extend to complete the extraction
Use the free leg as a posting tool to accelerate rotation and control landing position
Immediately secure offensive grips upon completing the roll to prevent opponent's recovery
setup_requirements: Leg Knot position established with opponent's control not fully consolidated
Opponent's grip on your trapped leg is loose or in transition between positions
Sufficient space exists between your shoulder and the mat to initiate rotation
Free leg available for posting and momentum generation
Upper body mobility maintained with hands free to post during roll

execution_steps.description: Identify the moment when opponent's control on your trapped leg weakens, typically during their transition attempts or grip adjustments. Confirm your shoulder has clearance to initiate rotation.
Plant your free hand and the same-side shoulder firmly on the mat, creating a stable rotation axis. Your free leg posts wide to generate rotational momentum and control direction.

Drive your posted shoulder into the mat and begin rotating your body over that shoulder. Keep your trapped leg completely relaxed and limp to minimize friction and allow it to slide through the entanglement.

Continue the rotation until your hips pass over your shoulders, using core tension to maintain a tight ball position. Your head should pass underneath your body as you rotate through the inverted position.

As you complete the rotation, explosively straighten your previously trapped leg to clear it from the entanglement. The rotational momentum combined with leg extension frees the leg from opponent's control.

Land with your hips facing opponent and immediately establish control grips on their legs. Transition to your preferred leg entanglement configuration or begin passing sequence before opponent can recover guard.

common_counters.counter: Opponent maintains tight grip on your heel/ankle throughout the roll, preventing extraction
common_counters.your_response: Abort the roll early and return to defensive positioning rather than completing rotation into worse position. Use the rotation to create distance and reset frames.

common_counters.counter: Opponent follows your rotation and maintains relative position, negating the reversal
common_counters.your_response: Accelerate through the second half of the rotation and immediately attack their legs as they follow. Their following motion often exposes their own legs to counter-entanglement.

common_counters.counter: Opponent recognizes setup and preemptively consolidates to Saddle position
common_counters.your_response: Switch to standard Saddle defense protocols. The Granby is no longer viable once opponent achieves dominant leg lock position. Address heel exposure first.

common_counters.counter: Opponent sprawls weight down to kill your momentum mid-roll
common_counters.your_response: Use the momentum pause to switch to a technical standup or seated guard recovery. The sprawl often opens space for alternative escapes.

common_errors.error: Initiating roll with stiff trapped leg
common_errors.consequence: The rigid leg catches on opponent's entanglement, stopping rotation and potentially worsening your position by giving opponent better purchase for submissions
common_errors.correction: Keep trapped leg completely limp and relaxed during initial rotation phase. Only extend the leg explosively during the final extraction moment.

common_errors.error: Rolling away from opponent instead of over the shoulder
common_errors.consequence: Exposes your back and potentially gives opponent back control, dramatically worsening your position from bad to catastrophic
common_errors.correction: Always roll over your shoulder toward the ceiling, not away from opponent. The rotation axis runs through your posted shoulder, not your spine.

common_errors.error: Attempting roll when opponent has consolidated grip on heel
common_errors.consequence: The roll tightens their heel hook grip and may accelerate the submission, resulting in a tap mid-rotation
common_errors.correction: Only attempt Granby when you've confirmed opponent's grip is loose or transitioning. If heel is secured, address that threat with standard defenses first.

common_errors.error: Failing to post free leg for momentum
common_errors.consequence: Insufficient rotational force to complete the roll, leaving you stuck mid-inversion in a worse position than you started
common_errors.correction: Drive aggressively off the posted free leg to generate enough momentum to complete the full rotation. Half-committed rolls consistently fail.

common_errors.error: Pausing between rotation completion and position consolidation
common_errors.consequence: Opponent recovers their leg control or guard position, negating your escape effort and returning to neutral or worse
common_errors.correction: Treat the roll and subsequent control establishment as one continuous motion. Any pause allows athletic opponents to recover.

training_progressions.description: Practice Granby rolls on open mat without partner. Focus on smooth shoulder rotation, maintaining tight body position, and landing in base. Perform 20 repetitions each direction daily to develop the movement pattern.

Partner establishes loose Leg Knot position and signals when to attempt roll. Focus on recognizing the correct moment to initiate and completing extraction smoothly. Partner provides no resistance but maintains position.

Partner maintains active Leg Knot position with moderate grip pressure. Practice identifying genuine windows for the Granby versus situations requiring alternative escapes. Begin connecting successful rolls to immediate top control.

Full resistance positional sparring starting from Leg Knot Bottom. Granby becomes one option in your escape toolkit. Track success rate and adjust timing based on live feedback. Integration with other escapes and reversals.

variants_and_adaptations.description: Instead of rolling to clear the entanglement, use the Granby momentum to immediately enter your own leg attack, transitioning from defensive to offensive without establishing neutral position first.
variants_and_adaptations.when_to_use: When opponent's legs are exposed during your rotation and you have confidence in your own leg lock game

variants_and_adaptations.variant_name: Modified Granby to single leg X
variants_and_adaptations.description: Abbreviated rotation that stops short of full reversal, using the momentum to establish Single Leg X-Guard rather than achieving top position. Maintains guard retention while escaping immediate danger.
variants_and_adaptations.when_to_use: When full reversal is unlikely due to opponent's athleticism or when you prefer guard play to top position

variants_and_adaptations.description: In no-gi, the lack of fabric grips makes the Granby more viable but also makes subsequent control more difficult. Focus on underhook and overhook establishment immediately upon completing rotation.
variants_and_adaptations.when_to_use: No-gi competition or training where gi grips are unavailable

knowledge_assessment.question: What is the primary goal of Granby roll to reverse position?
knowledge_assessment.answer: The primary goal is to use rotational momentum to disengage your trapped leg from the opponent's leg entanglement and achieve top position. This transforms a defensive situation into an offensive opportunity by completely reversing the positional hierarchy of the Leg Knot position.

knowledge_assessment.question: What position do you start Granby roll to reverse position from?
knowledge_assessment.answer: This technique starts from Leg Knot Bottom, specifically when the opponent has established a leg entanglement but has not yet consolidated into a fully dominant position like Saddle. The transitional nature of Leg Knot creates the windows necessary for the Granby to succeed.

knowledge_assessment.question: What are the key grips needed for Granby roll to reverse position?
knowledge_assessment.answer: Unlike many techniques, the Granby roll requires releasing grips rather than establishing them. Your hands should be free to post on the mat during rotation. The critical contact points are your posting shoulder on the mat and your free leg posting to generate momentum. After completing the roll, immediately establish control grips on opponent's legs.

knowledge_assessment.question: How do you counter an opponent's Granby roll attempt from Leg Knot Top?
knowledge_assessment.answer: The most effective counter is maintaining constant grip pressure on the trapped heel or ankle throughout any movement. If you feel opponent initiating rotation, consolidate toward Saddle position to eliminate the escape window. Alternatively, follow their rotation while maintaining grip, which negates the reversal and often worsens their position.

knowledge_assessment.question: When is the best time to attempt Granby roll to reverse position?
knowledge_assessment.answer: The optimal timing is during your opponent's grip transitions or positional adjustments when their control momentarily weakens. Specifically, look for moments when they are switching between heel hook and toe hold grips, adjusting their leg position for a different entanglement, or when they overcommit to an attack attempt.

knowledge_assessment.question: Your opponent maintains a grip on your ankle during your Granby attempt - how should you adjust?
knowledge_assessment.answer: If you recognize the maintained grip early in rotation, abort immediately and return to standard defensive frames. Completing the roll with a trapped ankle often worsens your position. If you're mid-roll, use the rotational momentum to attempt a limp leg extraction by relaxing completely and letting the leg slide through their grip. If extraction fails, use the new angle to establish different defensive frames.

knowledge_assessment.question: What hip and shoulder mechanics are critical for successful execution?
knowledge_assessment.answer: The shoulders must lead the rotation - drive the posting shoulder firmly into the mat to create a stable rotation axis. Keep hips tight to your chest in a ball position during mid-roll. The critical mechanic is rotating OVER your shoulder toward the ceiling, not sideways away from opponent. Hip mobility allows the compact position necessary for clean rotation.

knowledge_assessment.question: After completing the Granby roll, what is your immediate positional priority?
knowledge_assessment.answer: Immediately establish control grips on opponent's legs before they can recover guard. Do not pause or celebrate the escape - treat the roll and control establishment as one continuous motion. Ideal follow-up is entering your own leg entanglement or initiating a guard pass, depending on how opponent's legs are positioned after your reversal.

knowledge_assessment.question: Why must the trapped leg remain limp during initial rotation?
knowledge_assessment.answer: A stiff leg catches on opponent's entanglement, creating friction that stops the rotation. The limp leg slides through gaps in the entanglement that wouldn't accommodate a rigid limb. Only after the rotation is complete should you explosively extend the leg to finalize extraction. This limp-then-extend sequencing is fundamental to the technique.

knowledge_assessment.question: How does the Granby roll to reverse position chain with other techniques if blocked?
knowledge_assessment.answer: If the Granby is blocked by opponent following your rotation, their movement often exposes their legs to counter-entanglement attacks. If blocked by sprawl pressure, the pause creates opportunity for technical standup or seated guard recovery. The key is recognizing early when the Granby won't succeed and transitioning to alternatives rather than forcing a failing technique.

safety_considerations: The Granby roll places significant stress on the neck and shoulders during the inverted rotation phase. Practitioners with cervical spine issues or shoulder injuries should avoid this technique until fully healed. Always warm up thoroughly before drilling, focusing on neck mobility and shoulder rotation. The rapid inversion can cause disorientation - progress gradually from slow technical repetitions to full-speed execution. When drilling with partners, ensure the training partner does not apply full submission pressure during your roll attempts, as completing a rotation while under heel hook pressure can cause knee injury. In live training, be prepared to tap if your roll attempt fails and opponent capitalizes with a submission - never prioritize the escape over your joint health.
position_integration: The Granby roll to reverse position occupies a specific niche within the leg entanglement defensive hierarchy. It is most effective in the transitional Leg Knot position before opponent consolidates to Saddle or Inside Ashi-Garami. The technique complements standard escape methods (hip escape, leg extraction, 50-50 counter-entangle) by providing an athletic option when technical escapes are unavailable. Understanding when to use the Granby versus other escapes is essential - it requires more athleticism but offers greater reward by achieving top position rather than merely escaping to neutral. The reversal connects directly to offensive leg lock entries, allowing practitioners to immediately threaten their own attacks after escaping danger.
